summary_oneline: CI has 3 currently-red jobs driven by 6 distinct, independently-verified root causes; the P0 resolver issue Copilot found is already fixed on dev.

constraints.statement: pyproject.toml already restricts uv's lock environments to linux/non-aarch64 specifically because of async-notify's wheel gap; this is the mechanism that already fixed the resolver-unsat issue.

test-wiki-extras / test-wiki-luau-fallback already establish the precedent this fix should follow: one job proves graceful degradation without an extra, a second job installs it and asserts nothing was silently skipped.
TargetedWriterToolkit (FEAT-543/TASK-3090) is a live, tested, documented feature in .claude/commands/sdd-start.md and .agents/skills/sdd-start/SKILL.md; only sdd-worker.md's copy regressed.

hypotheses.statement: P0 (async-notify/aarch64 resolver unsat) is already fixed on dev as of commit 6e10be590 (today).

test-core's mass collection failures are caused by two independent bugs: (a) an unconditional tqdm import in core crew.py, and (b) ci.yml never being updated after FEAT-523 split 15 LLM-client packages out of core.

test-wiki-extras' pymupdf failures stem from a genuine mismatch between the FEAT-451 spec (which assumes pymupdf is a core dependency) and pyproject.toml (which only exposes it via the bookstore extra) — needs a spec-time decision, not a unilateral fix.

test-tool-optimizations' 4 failures are a documentation regression: FEAT-549's Orchestrator Loop rewrite of sdd-worker.md dropped FEAT-543's Delegated-implementation section that its sibling host docs still carry.

Two additional test-wiki-extras/test-core failures (schema-version literal, BASE_CSS symbol) are ordinary test staleness from later, unrelated features (FEAT-557, FEAT-493) and are fixable without touching source.

unknowns.question: Should pymupdf/pymupdf4llm become unconditional core dependencies of ai-parrot (matching the FEAT-451 spec's stated assumption), or should wiki PDF ingestion degrade gracefully and the spec's claim be corrected?
Should the new CI coverage for the 15 ai-parrot-client-* satellites be one combined job (sync all + run tests/clients/) or per-provider jobs matching the existing test-tools/test-loaders granularity?

Should the F006c stale-symbol drift bugs (DatabaseAgentToolkit, DatabaseAgent, 'flows' from parrot.bots, FAISSStore) get their own dedicated investigation/task, or be folded into the same spec as F006a/b?

recommended_next_command.rationale: Six root causes are independently localized with high confidence and are individually small, well-bounded fixes (one lazy-import guard, one new CI job + several importorskip guards, one dependency-placement decision, one doc restoration, two stale-test corrections). This is task decomposition, not architecture exploration.
